summary: No test changed this round, and I established that by measurement rather than by accepting the claim. ReviewRoundCapTest.java is byte-identical to the bytes I passed at round 8 (sha256 edcb4440d272), and the only change to the production code the suite covers is a five-line comment block in check-reviewed.sh -- proven by diffing the staged files against the round-8 index blobs recovered from git's dangling objects, not by reading the author's summary. Baseline is 15/15 green against today's staged bytes, and both mutations that closed the round-6/7 majors still fail exactly the tests that were written for them. M4.31's row describes the T8 deletion arm accurately; I reproduced the exploit end to end. Nothing got worse. No new findings.
notes: STAGED HASH verified as 8844d8c663c6 before starting and again immediately before recording. NOTHING IN THE WORKING TREE WAS EDITED: all mutation was done in an isolated copy under a private scratch dir (gradlew, gradle/, settings.gradle.kts, .gitignore, scripts/, baselines/, buildSrc/), and `git status --porcelain -- scripts/ buildSrc/ docs/ baselines/` shows only the staged entries with a clean worktree column, before and after.

(1) THE 'NOTHING CHANGED' CLAIM IS VERIFIED, NOT ACCEPTED, and the method matters because no packet or stored diff exists for round 8 -- .harness/review holds only verdict JSON, and there is no packet-M4.21 file. I recovered the round-8 INDEX BLOBS from `git fsck --dangling`: an unreachable blob is exactly what a superseded `git add` leaves behind. RESULT: the round-8 check-reviewed.sh is blob e0d0e2ad, and `diff` against the staged file is ONE HUNK -- the 3-line `NF > 1` heading replaced by the 5-line non-space-remainder heading. Zero executable lines differ; every executable line below it shifts by exactly +2, which independently corroborates round 8's own citation of the awk selector at check-reviewed.sh:142 against its position at :144 today.

(1a) THE TEST FILE IS GENUINELY UNTOUCHED, by two independent arguments. First, absence: dangling copies of ReviewRoundCapTest.java exist at 283, 349, 416, 421 and 482 lines, and NONE matches the staged 492-line file -- had the file been edited after round 8, round 8's version would necessarily be sitting there unreachable, and it is not. Second, positive identification: the 482-line dangling blob is round 7's (it still carries the inert `"decoy\n"` fixture and the stale 'uniquely pins HISTORY' comment that round 7 filed as T6 and T7), and the staged file carries the round-8 fixes for both, at exactly the lines round 8's own notes cite -- the revised subset comment at 355-366 and T8's citation of :464 landing inside aROUNDSLineAppearingOnlyAsDIFFCONTEXT, the test T8 names as a neighbouring arm.

(1b) review_rounds.py: both dangling versions differ from staged only inside the module docstring (the nearest, a6af352b, by one sentence -- 'before the count is compared' becoming 'before the count is REFUSED (not before it is compared...)'). No executable line differs on any candidate, so the conclusion holds regardless of which one is round 8's.

(2) BASELINE 15/15 GREEN on today's staged bytes, confirmed twice (before the sweep and after restoring the gate, with `cmp` against the staged bytes in between): tests=15 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0 from TEST-binjava.ReviewRoundCapTest.xml. The worktree copies of all three files are byte-identical to the index (`git diff --name-only -- scripts/ buildSrc/` is empty), which matters because the fixture copies the scripts from `Path.of("..")` -- the worktree, not the index -- so the suite is genuinely exercising the bytes under review.

(2a) BOTH ROUND-6/7 MAJORS STAY CLOSED, re-measured rather than carried forward. Dropping ` -- baselines/review.txt` from the gate's `git diff --cached` -> 2 failures: anArgumentInADIFFERENTSTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap and aFILENAMEThatMerelyMATCHESTheGuardAsAPatternDoesNOTLiftTheCap. Replacing the no-task guard at line 97 with `if false` -> 1 failure: verdictsThatNameNOTASKRefuseRatherThanCountingAsROUNDZERO. Each is the test named for that defect, so neither is refusing for an incidental reason.

(3) M4.31's ROW DESCRIBES THE DELETION ARM CORRECTLY, and I checked every factual claim in it rather than the prose. 'Widening the awk selector from /^\+/ to /^[-+]/ leaves all fifteen tests green' -- re-measured, 15/15, unchanged from round 8, so T8 did not get better or worse. 'A staged DELETION of a rounds:<task> line then argues the cap' -- REPRODUCED END TO END rather than reasoned about: a scratch repo with `rounds:M9.1  argued earlier, now stale` committed, that line then `git rm --cached`'d, four rounds recorded, and the MUTANT gate prints "WARN ... ARGUED as 'rounds:M9.1'" and exits 0. The same fixture against the UNMUTATED staged gate FAILs with the cap message and exits 1, which confirms T8's own grading: production behaviour today is correct and only the test coverage of that arm is absent. 'Reachable rather than equivalent' is therefore accurate. The row is a sufficient specification for whoever implements the staged-vs-HEAD primitive.

(4) THE RECORDED MINORS DID NOT GET WORSE, and this needs no re-sweep: T3, T4, T5 and T8 are all mutations of check-reviewed.sh, whose executable lines are byte-identical to the ones round 8 measured (see note 1), against a test file that is byte-identical (note 1a). Behaviour cannot have moved. T8 was re-measured anyway, above, and is unchanged. Not re-filed, per review.md rule 11.

(5) ONE EQUIVALENT MUTANT MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, on the same reasoning round 8 used for the comment-skip arm. Replacing the shipped reason check `rest ~ /[^[:space:]]/` with awk's BUILT-IN `NF > 1` survives 15/15 green -- but it is equivalent, not a hole, and I verified the equivalence rather than assuming it: given `f[1] == k` has already matched, `NF > 1` holds exactly when a second non-blank token exists, which is exactly when the stripped remainder contains a non-space character. No input distinguishes them. Not a finding.

(5a) A MEASUREMENT ABOUT THE ONE COMMENT THAT CHANGED, offered to the author rather than filed, because the direction of the error is safe. The new heading says `NF > 1` 'was tried and is broken: a trailing tab splits into a second, EMPTY field'. Measured with awk directly on `+rounds:M9.1<TAB>`: `split(line, f, /[[:space:]]+/)` returns 2 with f[2] empty -- so the described MECHANISM is real and the warning is sound if 'NF' means that split count. Awk's built-in NF for the same record is 1, because default-FS splitting strips trailing blanks -- so read literally, built-in `NF > 1` is not broken but equivalent (note 5). Not filed: the surrounding awk uses `split()` three lines down, a reader in context reads the count as that one, and M4.26's row propagates the warning in the SAFE direction (do not use it), so the worst outcome is an implementer choosing the more explicit strip-and-check that already shipped.

(6) NO TEST DEPENDS ON THE DOCUMENTATION IN THIS ROUND. The suite asserts on the gate's exit status and printed output only; review.md appears in ReviewRoundCapTest solely inside comments (lines 171, 189, 201, 278), never in a fixture or an assertion. So review.md rule 12 and the backlog rows cannot have loosened any assertion, and no assertion text was weakened -- the file is unchanged, which is the strongest form of that check.
(7) ALL 15 RED RECORDS PRESENT in .harness/tdd/red.json, one per test method, names matching the 15 in the file. Unchanged file means unchanged keys, so no re-run was owed.

TIER AND STANDARDS: unchanged from round 8 and still correct. The subject under test IS a shell gate over a git index, so exec'ing bash and git is the behaviour being constrained, not I/O smuggled into business logic -- non-negotiable 7 is not engaged. No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no mock, no clock. The @TempDir-resolves-to-system-temp point against testing.md rule 17 remains pre-existing and repo-wide, and still belongs in a standards row rather than as a finding against M4.21.
